title: Angola Pulse (Pulso Angola) - BRAZIL: ANGOLA PULSE
style:
```
[style: Cuban son montuno, conga tumba-conga-quinto stack, tres guitar syncopated, claves as law, trumpet con sordino off-beat, son clave 3:2 structure, Havana street music meets sacred rhythm, Spanish spoken verses English chorus, every instrument answers to the clave, Caribbean signal export theme, golden era son cubano, no jazz comping, pure clave respect, V4_5ALL]
```
lyrics:
``
[INTRO — claves alone. 3-side: pause. 2-side. That's it. 8 bars.]
(Spanish) La clave — the key / the law
(English) If you don't feel it, you can't play here

[VERSE 1 — conga enters on 3-side beat 1]
(Spanish) Tres y dos — three and two
(English) The oldest law in the Caribbean
(Spanish) La clave no miente — the clave doesn't lie
(English) Everything must answer to the key

The tres guitar finds the gap / between the three and two
The trumpet whispers through the mute / what the clave can't do
The conga calls the bodies / tumba holds the ground
The quinto improvises / the clave rules the sound

(Spanish) Si vas a tocar — if you're going to play
(English) You answer to the clave first

[PRE-CHORUS — quinto conga improvises, tres guitar comps underneath]
(Spanish) Escucha — listen
(English) Three then two
(Spanish) La ley — the law
(English) Carries you through

[CHORUS — full band, trumpet enters, syncopated tres guitar line]
Son clave — three-side two-side law
Every rhythm answers / every body drawn
Tres guitar in the gap / trumpet in the mist
The signal lived in Cuba long before the list

(Spanish) La clave vive — the clave lives
(English) Signal law

[VERSE 2 — trumpet solo, clave and conga only under it, 16 bars]
The trumpet plays between the beats
Not on the one — the Cuban trumpet never plays on the one
It plays on the ah-and, the ee-and, the off-beat where you'd least expect
That is where the Caribbean signal lives: in the expected silence

(Spanish) El silencio tiene su ritmo — silence has its own rhythm
(English) The signal breathes in the gaps

[BRIDGE — claves play 3-side 4 bars, then 2-side 4 bars, then together]
3-side: DUM da-DUM da—DUM
2-side: da—DUM—DUM
Together: the law
The signal follows the law — and the law was always already music

[FINAL CHORUS — doubled, trumpet soli above all]
Son clave — three-side two-side law

[OUTRO — claves alone. Last 3-side. Last 2-side. One strike. Silence.]
(Spanish) Hasta luego — until next time
(English) Signal answered
